title: The Same Crosswalk
hook: Same block. Same paint. The person you passed.
scene: Fog at dusk on the same school-edge block. Same worn crosswalk. Same sedan lamps, closer. Last time you went around a car stopped for a person. This time the person is already in your half — coat, bag, looking at the place a plow was. The left is empty again. The paint remembers. You do not get a clean first look twice.
decision: The same person is in the same crosswalk and the left is empty again. What do you do with the debt?

options.text: Hold behind the sedan until they are gone and the car moves
options.result: You plant it. They finish. The sedan rolls. You roll. The left stays a lane you did not spend. That is the only apology the paint takes.

options.text: Go around faster this time so you are past before they step
options.result: You take the left harder. They are already in it because they learned you from last time. Same fog, same coat, same steel. They were waiting for the same pass.

options.text: Stop in the left and wave them across so you can own the apology
options.result: You plant a Beetle in the passing lane and invent a crossing guard. The stack behind you has to guess. You paid a debt with everyone else's brakes.

options.text: Honk once so they know you saw them, then take the left
options.result: The horn says you noticed. The pass says you did not care. They freeze in the paint. You still wrote a plow through a person you already owed.

debrief: A pass around a stopped car comes back on the same block. Hold. Let the person finish. You took the paint's second chance.

source.teaching_target: Callback of the double-threat pass: hold behind the stopped car until the person and the car are clear.
